short: Swedish colonial settlement in North America along the Delaware River.
full:
Established in March 1638 under the direction of the Swedish South Company, New Sweden was a colonial settlement located along the lower reaches of the Delaware River in present-day United States. Centered around Fort Christina, it aimed to secure a foothold in the lucrative North American fur and tobacco trade.

Though never heavily populated, the colony introduced European farming techniques and log cabin construction to the region. It maintained relatively peaceful relations with the local Lenape people but struggled with lack of support from the homeland. In 1655, the colony was captured by the Dutch Republic and incorporated into New Netherland, ending Sweden's ambitions in North America.
